card.name: Small words in opioid warning sentences
card.fires_on: Small linking words (the, for, may, with) inside fixed boxed-warning sentences of opioid cough and pain labels, just before the main risk or benefit phrase.

modes.label: After 'for whom'
modes.description: The word 'the' in 'for use in adult patients for whom the benefits of cough suppression...'.
modes.example: Oral Solution (Syrup) for use in adult patients for whom<< the>> benefits of cough suppression are expected to outweigh

modes.label: After CNS depressants list
modes.description: The word 'may' after 'including alcohol,' in the opioid-benzodiazepine warning.
modes.example: Concomitant use of opioids with benzodiazepines or other central nervous system (CNS) depressants, including alcohol,<< may>> result in profound sedation, respiratory depression

modes.label: Other linking words
modes.description: Words like 'for' or 'with' before an anticholinergic or monitoring phrase.
modes.example: Evaluate patients<< for>> signs of urinary retention or reduced gastric mot

card.writes: Little clear effect; it suppresses code-like tokens and promotes opening brackets, which are unrelated to this text.
card.plain: It marks the small connecting word in stock opioid warning sentences, right before the risk or benefit is stated.
